newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech non-finance firms H1 profit down 18.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech non-finance firms H1 profit down 18.8 pct.

text.p: First half gross profit created by Czech non-financial corporations fell 18.8 percent, year-on-year, the Czech National Bank said in a report obtained on Monday.

In its soon-to-be-released October Commentary on Economic and Monetary Development, the CNB said non-finance companies pre-tax profits fell in nominal terms to 12.5 billion crowns to 54.1 billion crowns. It did not give similar results for banks and financial corporations.
"In profit-making companies, economic performance dropped from 91.7 billion crowns in (first half 1995) to 84.5 billion crowns in (first half 1996)," the CNB report said.

It said the lower earnings at profit-making companies were due, among other things, to the creation of reserves for bad loans, which grew in year-on-year terms by 16.4 billion crowns to 231.5 billion crowns at the end of the second half 1996.
In losing companies, the loss volume rose to 30.4 billion crowns from 25.1 billion crowns and losses were recorded in about "two-fifths of all companies," it said.

The CNB said that in addition to reserves creation, "this poor performance was brought about by lower output caused by growing competition on foreign markets, a decline in external demand, and lower export prices.

"This was particularly seen in the paper and celluose industry where output fell by 5.3 percent in year-on-year terms, the textile and clothing industry (-5.2 percent) and the leather industry (-4.5 percent)," the report added.
It said that the economic performance of particularly agricultural, construction and building materials production firms was adversely affected by the long winter.
